surface_mechanism_description: The formation of nanoscale clusters on CdTe epilayers is attributed to two mechanisms: (1) the development of CdTe oxidation, which initiates the creation of 3D oxide islands, and (2) an Ostwald ripening process between these clusters. The oxidation of the CdTe surface induces the formation of a thin oxide layer, which undergoes a 2D/3D transition due to its different lattice parameter, leading to nanoclustering. The Ostwald ripening process involves mass transfer via surface diffusion of adatoms, where larger clusters incorporate material from smaller, less stable ones.
evidence: The oxidation of the CdTe surface induces the formation of a thin oxide layer which undergoes, due to its very different lattice parameter (e.g. a=4.805 Å for TeO2), a 2D/3D transition leading to a nanoclustering of the surface. This oxidation appears then to be the driving force of the nanoscale clustering: the initial oxidation of the CdTe surface induces the formation of a thin oxide layer which undergoes, due to its very different lattice parameter (e.g. a=4.805 Å for TeO2), a 2D/3D transition leading to a nanoclustering of the surface. In an Ostwald ripening process, the mass transfer occurs in a closed system by an exchange between the clusters via the surface diffusion of adatoms; the larger clusters continually incorporate material on behalf of the smaller ones which are less stable.
